Heard from the TV: "Your council plans to replace a bus line with free e-scooters to cut emissions. How would you persuade a green-minded councillor that this could still be a mistake?"
steps.thought: Good topic; I'll give a structured persuasive answer.

args.text: I understand that e-scooters look green, but I think replacing the bus line could still be a mistake. Firstly, a bus carries many people at once, whereas a scooter carries only one, so the emissions per person may not fall as much as expected. Secondly, elderly people, parents with children and people with disabilities can't use scooters, so they would be left without transport. Also, scooters are not used in bad weather, and if people eventually go back to their cars, the pollution will be even higher. I would suggest a trial period first, and keeping the bus line until the results are clear.
